Subject: POC trial planning & workload intake - Acme Health

Hi Sarah —

Great to meet you and Alex this morning. Quick recap and suggested next steps from our call:

1) Success criteria (we agreed to draft):
   - Latency: 95th percentile < 350ms for standard clinical note generation
   - Accuracy: match or exceed current rule-based extraction on the evaluation prompt set (TBD)%
   - Cost: target <$0.002 / 1k tokens for evaluation window

2) Evaluation plan:
   - 2-week POC with your 5 representative workloads (notes ingestion pipeline + anonymized sample)
   - Weekly checkpoints (Wed) to review metrics and sample outputs

3) Timeline / ownership:
   - Redwood: provide POC infra, workload intake template, initial config (Ben & Marissa) — target start Mon Jun 28
   - Acme Health: share workload samples + security questionnaire answers (Sarah / Alex) by Thu Jun 24

4) Workload intake items we need today:
   - Expected RPS during trial (avg/peak)
   - Typical and max token lengths (prompt + completion)
   - Concurrent sessions / users and expected burst patterns
   - Any rate-limiting or tokenization peculiarities in your pre-processing

I attached a draft POC plan and a quick workload intake template (workload-intake-template.xlsx). Can you fill the intake sheet for the 5 workloads and return by Thu? Once we have that, Marissa will size the Dedicated pool and I’ll provide a runbook for internal testing.

Thanks — looking forward to getting started.

Best,
Ben

Ben —

Thanks for the notes and the plan. Quick answers inline:

- We can target Jun 28 start but need to confirm legal sign-off on the DPA (in progress).
- Workload intake: I started the spreadsheet and uploaded two sample files (anonymized).
  - Avg RPS: 3 requests/sec for our primary workflow, peak 25 RPS during batch backfills
  - Typical token lengths: prompts ~120 tokens, expected completions ~420 tokens (avg total ~540). Max observed per document ~2,400 tokens.
  - Concurrency: ~8 concurrent active sessions; spikes to 40 during morning syncs for 10-15 minutes

I’ll finish the intake for all 5 workloads and send by Thu. Also looping Alex on infra questions.

Thanks Sarah — that data is super helpful. A few follow-ups to make sure sizing and evaluation are aligned:

- Given the 2,400 token max and peak 25 RPS, for the POC we recommend starting with a 3-GPU Dedicated pool (A100-equivalent) with autoscale to 5 for burst windows. Marissa will confirm cost estimates.
- For evaluation accuracy, can you share the evaluation prompt set (20–30 labeled cases) that you use for the rule-based baseline? If you can’t share labels, even an unlabeled sample set would help with qualitative review.
- Can you confirm whether backfills are staggered (queue-based) or run-from-origin (all-at-once)? That affects burst padding and cache warmup approach.

Next steps from our side:
- Marissa to provide initial sizing + ballpark trial pricing (by EOD Tue)
- I’ll draft a mutual action plan (MAP) with milestones and checkpoints and share the Doc (will include HubSpot deal link)

Marissa — could you size and add cost guidance based on Sarah’s traffic notes?

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Hi all —

Sizing summary (initial estimate):
- Baseline: 3 x A100-equivalent GPUs (handles avg 3 RPS with headroom)
- Burst sizing: autoscale to 5 GPUs to cover 25 RPS peak for short windows (~10–15m)
- Memory/kv cache: 64GB aggregate to keep common prefixes warm for clinical note templates

Estimated POC cost (2-week window): $5,800 (compute + monitoring + support) — includes 3 weekly checkpoints and one fine-tuning pass if needed.

Attachments: detailed sizing worksheet (workload-intake-template.xlsx updated). I also added columns for concurrency, warmup strategy, and evaluation prompt link.
